statement: A bound Var(F_n) <= C n/log(n), by itself, does not imply any bound Var(F_n) <= C_delta n^(1-delta) for fixed delta>0.
assumptions: n>=2; fixed finite C>0 and delta>0; no additional model information.
source: Independent elementary derivation; C0120 job describes a power improvement beyond a logarithmic bound.
proof: Take v_n=n/log(n). Then v_n/n^(1-delta)=n^delta/log(n) tends to infinity. No finite C_delta dominates this sequence.
remaining_gap: This is a logical obstruction for sequences of bounds, not an example of an actual polymer free energy. Exact C0120 model and current literature still need recovery.

statement: The cited Chatterjee 2008 Section 8 theorem bounds the variance of a free-endpoint Gaussian up-right path maximum in Z^2, not an arbitrary-dimensional positive-temperature log partition function.
source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.4221; local problems.jsonl line 120 and sources.jsonl line 29.
source_quote: Improve the fluctuation exponent in directed polymers.
proof: Source model and Theorem 8.1 read directly; Section 12(2) separately lists dimension >=3 chaos as open. See SOURCE_STATUS.json.
remaining_gap: Current openness and possible later extensions not certified.

statement: For the source-model maximum M_n with degree-k Gaussian chaos masses v_nk, Var(M_n)<=sum_{k<=K}v_nk+n/(K+1). A bound on the sum through K=ceil(n^delta) of order n^(1-delta) implies the same power variance bound.
assumptions: iid standard Gaussian weights, n vertices per path, finite free-endpoint up-right paths, 0<delta<1.
proof: Hermite Dirichlet form sum k v_nk=n, then bound the tail by n/(K+1).
remaining_gap: No bound on polynomial-degree low-chaos mass has been proved.

statement: For the source model, M_n=sum_t A_t+M_n(R), with A_t the Gaussian average of the t+1 vertices in layer t and R the within-layer centered environment; Var(M_n)=H_n+Var(M_n(R)).
assumptions: iid N(0,1), n vertices from the origin moving up/right, free endpoint.
proof: Every path visits one vertex per layer; zero cross covariance and joint Gaussianity make all layer averages jointly independent of all residuals.
remaining_gap: Residual variance is unbounded by this argument; residual coordinates are correlated.

statement: Fixed-degree chaos suppression and fixed-positive-noise gradient decorrelation, even with Gaussian Dirichlet energy n, do not imply a power variance bound.
assumptions: General Gaussian Sobolev functions; the functions in this counterexample are not convex or globally Lipschitz.
proof: F_n=sqrt(n/ceil(log n)) H_{ceil(log n)}(G), normalized Hermite polynomials; variance n/ceil(log n), Dirichlet energy n, gradient covariance ratio exp(-(ceil(log n)-1)u).
remaining_gap: Scope excludes actual polymer maxima; stronger geometric control is supplied separately by the fan example.

statement: A sequence of iid-Gaussian n-vertex layered path maxima can be convex, sqrt(n)-Lipschitz, have path-indicator gradients of squared norm n, and exhibit chaos at noise u_n=16 log log n/log n, while Var(M_n)>=c n/log n and therefore has no fixed power improvement.
assumptions: Fan graph with n disjoint branches of n-1 vertices and a common root; graph degree grows with n. This is not the fixed Z^2 lattice.
proof: Independent root Gaussian plus sqrt(n-1) times a maximum of n Gaussians; separated quantile events and Mills bounds give a c/log n variance lower bound for that maximum; a bivariate Gaussian tail union bound gives the vanishing-noise overlap estimate.
remaining_gap: Independent proof audit pending. No impossibility for the source lattice is asserted.

statement: Qualitative overlap decay O_n(n^(-1/4))=o(n), even for convex sqrt(n)-Lipschitz Gaussian n-vertex path maxima with Dirichlet energy n, does not by itself imply any fixed power variance saving.
assumptions: Changing graph with r_n=floor(n/log n) mandatory common vertices and m_n=ceil(exp(sqrt(n))) disjoint branches of n-r_n vertices; iid N(0,1); n sufficiently large. This is not the Z^2 model or a bounded-degree graph.
proof: Independent common-prefix Gaussian variance is r_n; a bivariate Gaussian tail bound makes maximizing branch indices decorrelate at u_n=n^(-1/4). Normalized overlap is r_n/n+o(1), but variance is at least r_n.
remaining_gap: Independent check pending. The common-prefix/growing-degree geometry is outside the parent problem.

statement: For a finite family of n-vertex directed paths with iid standard Gaussian weights and a unique maximum, if O_n(n^(-a))<=C n^(1-b) for fixed a,b>0 and finite C independent of n, then Var(M_n)<=(1+C)n^(1-min(a,b)).
assumptions: Distinct path vertex sets; finite path family; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck environment coupling; iid standard Gaussian weights; fixed positive a and b; uniform overlap bound.
source: Independent integral split; Gaussian covariance identity verified in Chatterjee arXiv:0810.4221v2 Lemma 3.3 and monotonicity in Lemma 3.5. See POLYNOMIAL_NOISE_QUANTIFIER.md.
proof: Var(M_n)=integral e^(-u)O_n(u)du; O_n<=n and is decreasing, so Var<=n t+O_n(t). Set t=n^(-a) and bound both terms.
remaining_gap: Neither the polynomial-noise scale nor polynomial overlap-magnitude bound is established for the source lattice.
